issue_request: FHIR-19571 was a Published FHIR-core conformance-rules change request resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. The submitter asked for a hint or link explaining what systems really support in the is-modifier text; the final resolution rejected a CapabilityStatement-style requirement and only directed replacing the obsolete Observation.reliability example with Observation.status of final.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites git commit 44ad3ffcf04a71a9affa02374a8596ac9ade7bfa. That commit updated source/conformance-rules.html and changed the is-modifier support example from observations with reliability other than ok to observations with status other than final; current blame for the example line still traces to that commit.
additional_context: conformance-rules.html is listed in publish.ini, and Observation is active in source/fhir.ini. The current Observation.status definition is a 1..1 modifier code whose listed statuses include final and entered-in-error, so the corrected example still references a live modifier element. Current source searches found no remaining Observation.reliability example, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. The current build-scope source already carries the approved status/final example and the surrounding wording correctly leaves support as implementation/business-rule behavior rather than requiring a CapabilityStatement declaration.
